title: Build a Stage 2 Computing Showcase
overview: Bring together everything from Stage 2 Computing into one showcase: a working program, the data behind it, a clear explanation of how it runs, and the safety rules you followed while making it.

project.drivingQuestion: How can I use the computing I learned in Stage 2 to build something that solves a real problem for someone in my community — and explain exactly how it works?
project.finalProduct: A working program or digital product, the plan and algorithm behind it, a test-and-debug log, a data display, and a spoken or written explanation of your design decisions.

stages.title: 1. Plan and decompose
stages.prompt: Choose a real problem. Using the ideas from Units 1, 2, 3, 4, break it into smaller parts and write the algorithm before you write any code.
stages.evidence: A decomposed problem and a written algorithm or flowchart

stages.title: 2. Build it
stages.prompt: Build your program or product using the tools from Units 5, 6, 7, 8. Build the smallest working version first, then add one feature at a time.
stages.evidence: A working program or digital product

stages.title: 3. Test, debug and improve
stages.prompt: Test your work against your success criteria. Keep a log of every bug: what you saw, what caused it, and how you fixed it.
stages.evidence: A test-and-debug log with at least three entries

stages.title: 4. Share it safely
stages.prompt: Present your showcase. Explain three design decisions, show your data, and say which online-safety rules from Units 9, 10, 11 you followed and why.
stages.evidence: A spoken, written or recorded explanation covering design, data and safety

evidenceChecklist: A decomposed problem with a written algorithm or flowchart
A working program or digital product
A test-and-debug log with at least three fixed bugs
Success criteria, each one ticked off with evidence
An explanation of your design decisions and the safety rules you followed

rubric.secure: The problem is decomposed, the algorithm is precise, and the pattern behind it is named.
The program runs, meets its criteria, and every bug found is logged with its cause and fix.
Data is collected accurately, organised sensibly and displayed so it answers a question.
Personal information is protected, sources are credited, and safety choices are explained.

questions.question: True or False: A computer can think by itself.
options: True
False
questions.answer: False
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: False (a computer only follows instructions; it cannot think by itself).

questions.question: What does “program” mean in computing?
options: The instructions inside a program — the blocks.
A free app where you join picture blocks to make a program.
A set of instructions that a computer can follow.
A person, animal or thing in ScratchJr that follows your blocks.
questions.answer: A set of instructions that a computer can follow.
questions.hint: Use the Unit 1 Computing Words reference.
questions.explanation: Program means a set of instructions that a computer can follow.

questions.question: Which computing word matches this meaning: To make the computer follow the program.?
